biography.plain_text: Keith Stotts is a Minnesota cabinetry executive who succeeded his father at Dura Supreme, becoming president and majority owner. He directed product development, manufacturing improvements and repeated factory expansion as the family business grew into a national custom-cabinet brand. The Stotts family sold the company to private-equity firm GHK Capital Partners in 2019.

long_biography.plain_text:
Curved cabinet doors capture Keith Stotts’s approach to Dura Supreme. When he suggested the idea to a product developer, the resulting prototype became an early example of the design and manufacturing work he pursued across the business. The company’s official history credits him with combining innovation, craftsmanship and value.

Stotts also controlled the financial decisions behind expansion. During one growth programme, conventional borrowing proved insufficient, so retained cash was channelled through a family investment company that could lend back to Dura Supreme. By the time the second-generation family sold the manufacturer, it employed hundreds of people and supplied custom cabinetry through dealers across the United States.
